ownership_reason: Only the gold holds the list of value types together with the decision for a class outside it; hops 1-4 pass the value and the type down and the result up and know nothing of which types are handled. On the trigger input (a String value for Integer.class) the gold returns null, which is not the value converted to the requested type that its javadoc promises ('@return the value of str converted to clazz'). The convention that a value which cannot be produced for the requested type is signalled by ParseException, never answered with null, is pinned outside the gold: TypeHandler.createClass and TypeHandler.createObject throw ParseException rather than returning null when the class is missing or cannot be instantiated; CommandLine.getParsedOptionValue documents '@throws ParseException if there are problems turning the option value into the desired type' and returns null only for an absent option or value, and CommandLine.getOptionObject yields null only after catching that ParseException; the passing tests testCreateValueClass_notFound, testCreateValueObject_unknownClass, testCreateValueURL_malformed and testCreateValueNumber_noNumber expect ParseException for values that cannot be converted. A caller that turns the gold's null into a ParseException relies on a null result the gold does not document and re-implements the gold's rejection one level up; it cannot even do so exactly, because above the gold a null result is ambiguous ((null, STRING_VALUE) legitimately converts to null, so a caller-side null check either still returns null for (null, Integer.class) or throws for (null, STRING_VALUE), where the correct configuration does the opposite). A caller that checks the class against the nine value types first is a second copy of the gold's dispatch list.
